text: Fill in the key pharmacological term in each statement about alcohol toxicity management.
questions: Fomepizole is a competitive inhibitor of *alcohol dehydrogenase/ADH:Which enzyme converts methanol to formaldehyde?* and is the first-line antidote for methanol poisoning.
Disulfiram inhibits *aldehyde dehydrogenase/ALDH:Which enzyme normally clears acetaldehyde?*, causing toxic acetaldehyde accumulation when ethanol is consumed.
In alcohol withdrawal, *benzodiazepines/BZDs/diazepam/lorazepam:Which drug class shares a receptor mechanism with ethanol?* are first-line because they provide cross-tolerance at the GABA-A receptor.
Folinic acid enhances the metabolism of *formate/formic acid:Which toxic metabolite of methanol damages the optic nerve?* to carbon dioxide via the tetrahydrofolate pathway.
Naltrexone is an *opioid/opioid receptor:Which receptor system mediates the rewarding effects of alcohol?* receptor antagonist that reduces alcohol craving by blocking endorphin-mediated reward.
